leads.summary: Initializers now select system starship and zoxide before mise exposes user-managed versions
leads.consequence: When a user's mise config puts a preferred starship or zoxide executable on PATH (for example [env] _.path, or a managed installation absent from the pre-activation PATH), the old order initializes those executables; the new order initializes the distro binaries first and only then changes PATH. In the sealed real-CLI run both post-init `command -v` results point to the managed executables, but only the baseline actually initialized them. Starship's init embeds its selected executable path in the generated prompt code, so a user who manages starship sees the system version in the prompt while invoking the managed CLI on PATH. Zoxide's initialized functions may come from a different version than subsequent zoxide calls. Preserve executable selection or establish an explicit tested policy for PATH/version skew.
leads.triage: behavioural; sent to Opus (followup-1 Q1); confirmed with synthetic wrappers, narrow (user must install starship/zoxide via mise); published as optional note

leads.summary: The new explanatory comment attributes hook loss to programs that preserve the original hook
leads.consequence: On the packaged versions, starship saves any existing PROMPT_COMMAND in STARSHIP_PROMPT_COMMAND and executes it inside starship_precmd; zoxide appends its hook to a string or array. Thus merely seeing an array without the mise hook as its own entry does not establish that it stopped executing. A controlled interactive shell with real binaries and an isolated global mise env value shows the base already runs mise's hook and exposes the configured value in a new shell, while the head also does. The issue report may have a different root cause, so do not promise this reordering repairs it on present dependencies without a reproducer on the current base. Correct the source comment and add a direct failing-before/passing-after test if this fixes a separate setup.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** mise's hook already runs at the base, so this does not fix #3685; after a second starship init the title stops updating.

### starship and zoxide keep mise's hook

starship moves mise's hook into `STARSHIP_PROMPT_COMMAND` and runs it each prompt; zoxide appends. mise's project env applied after `cd` at both commits. **Impact:** #3685's cause stays unknown, and the new comment is wrong.

**Suggested change:** Keep the current order; ask the reporters for `declare -p STARSHIP_PROMPT_COMMAND` and `type -a python` from an affected shell.

<details><summary>Reproducer (passes at the merge-base and at the head)</summary>

Tools: bash 5.3.15, mise 2026.9.14, starship 1.26.0, zoxide 0.10.0 (Arch extra at the PR date: mise 2026.9.9 with the same PROMPT_COMMAND code, starship 1.26.0, zoxide 0.10.0). Run in an isolated sandbox with a private HOME.

Save as `test/shell.d/bash-init-mise-hook-test.sh` and run `bash test/shell.d/bash-init-mise-hook-test.sh` in a checkout. It needs real `mise`, `starship` and `zoxide` on PATH and skips otherwise.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(dirname "$0")/base-test.sh"

# Runs default/bash/init in a real interactive bash with the real mise, starship
# and zoxide, then checks that mise's prompt hook applies a project's env after a
# plain `builtin cd` (what the `cd` alias's zd function uses), i.e. that the hook
# still fires on the next prompt.
for cmd in mise starship zoxide; do
  command -v "$cmd" >/dev/null || { skip "needs $cmd on PATH"; exit 0; }
done

tmpdir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmpdir"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$tmpdir/home" "$tmpdir/project" "$tmpdir/etc-mise" "$tmpdir/tmp"
: >"$tmpdir/starship.toml"
printf '[env]\nMISE_PROBE = "project"\n' >"$tmpdir/project/mise.toml"

run_interactive() {
  local term="$1" script="$2"
  env -i PATH="$PATH" TERM="$term" COLUMNS=80 HOME="$tmpdir/home" TMPDIR="$tmpdir/tmp" \
    XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$tmpdir/home/.config" XDG_DATA_HOME="$tmpdir/home/.local/share" \
    XDG_STATE_HOME="$tmpdir/home/.local/state" XDG_CACHE_HOME="$tmpdir/home/.cache" \
    MISE_SYSTEM_CONFIG_DIR="$tmpdir/etc-mise" MISE_TRUSTED_CONFIG_PATHS="$tmpdir/project" \
    STARSHIP_CONFIG="$tmpdir/starship.toml" OMARCHY_PATH="$ROOT" PROJECT="$tmpdir/project" \
    bash --norc --noprofile -i <<<"$script" 2>/dev/null
}

# Arch's /etc/bash.bashrc adds a title entry for xterm*/alacritty*/foot*/tmux*,
# which makes PROMPT_COMMAND an array; TERM=linux leaves it a plain string.
script='[[ $TERM == xterm* ]] && PROMPT_COMMAND+=('"'"'printf "\033]0;%s\007" "$PWD"'"'"')
source "$OMARCHY_PATH/default/bash/init"
builtin cd "$PROJECT"
echo "probe=${MISE_PROBE-unset}"
exit'

for term in xterm-256color linux; do
  output=$(run_interactive "$term" "$script")
  [[ $output == *"probe=project"* ]] || fail "mise prompt hook applies the project env after cd (TERM=$term)" "output: $output"
  pass "mise prompt hook applies the project env after cd (TERM=$term)"
done
```

## Actual output

Merge-base c5b4db77 (mise activated before starship and zoxide):

```

ok - mise prompt hook applies the project env after cd (TERM=linux)
```

PR head a806bfee:

```

```

Control that the test can fail: merge-base init with one line appended, `unset STARSHIP_PROMPT_COMMAND` (simulates the hook being dropped):

```
output: \e]0;/tmp/omarchy\a\e]0;/tmp/omarchy\a\e]0;/tmp/work/tmp.O9NdBAqpRJ/project\aprobe=unset
\e]0;/tmp/work/tmp.O9NdBAqpRJ/project\a
not ok - mise prompt hook applies the project env after cd (TERM=xterm-256color)
```

(`\e` and `\a` stand for the ESC and BEL bytes of the title sequence.)

## Where the hook is at the merge-base

In an interactive bash with TERM=xterm-256color, after a copy of Arch's `/etc/bash.bashrc`, `default/bash/shell`, `aliases`, `functions` and `init` at c5b4db77 were sourced, then `builtin cd` into a directory whose `mise.toml` sets `MISE_PROBE = "project"` and `_.path = ["{{config_root}}/bin"]` (separate run with the review fixture; actual output, title escape sequences removed):

```
@@ PC_DECL=declare -a PROMPT_COMMAND=([0]="starship_precmd" [1]="printf \"\\033]0;%s@%s:%s\\007\" \"\${USER}\" \"\${HOSTNAME%%.*}\" \"\${PWD/#\$HOME/\\~}\"" [2]="__zoxide_hook")
@@ SPC_DECL=declare -- STARSHIP_PROMPT_COMMAND="_mise_hook_prompt_command"
@@ PROBE_BEFORE_CD=unset
@@ PROBE_AFTER_CD=project PROJECT_BIN_ON_PATH=yes
@@ PROBE_AFTER_LEAVE=unset PROJECT_BIN_ON_PATH=no
```

The PROMPT_COMMAND array is the one quoted in #3685 for Omarchy 4.0.0. `starship init bash` moved mise's entry into `STARSHIP_PROMPT_COMMAND`, and `starship_precmd` runs it with `eval "$STARSHIP_PROMPT_COMMAND"` before it renders the prompt (starship `src/init/starship.bash`, lines 68-70 and 129-135 at v1.26.0).

</details>

### A second starship init drops the terminal title

starship checks only PROMPT_COMMAND element 0, now mise's hook, so a user's own starship init or `source ~/.bashrc` re-registers it and overwrites `STARSHIP_PROMPT_COMMAND`, which holds Arch's title entry. **Impact:** the terminal title stops updating.

**Suggested change:** Keep mise before starship.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at a806bfee)</summary>

Tools: bash 5.3.15, mise 2026.9.14, starship 1.26.0, zoxide 0.10.0, run in an isolated sandbox with a private HOME.

A second `eval "$(starship init bash)"` happens when a user keeps starship's own `~/.bashrc` line, or re-sources `~/.bashrc`. Starship only checks whether `$PROMPT_COMMAND` (element 0 of the array) contains `starship_precmd`. At the head, element 0 is `_mise_hook_prompt_command`, so starship registers itself again and overwrites `STARSHIP_PROMPT_COMMAND`, which at the head holds the terminal-title entry.

Save as `test/shell.d/bash-init-starship-reinit-test.sh` and run `bash test/shell.d/bash-init-starship-reinit-test.sh` in a checkout. It needs real `mise`, `starship` and `zoxide` on PATH and skips otherwise. The `printf "<title>"` entry stands in for the title entry Arch's `/etc/bash.bashrc` adds for xterm*, alacritty*, foot* and tmux* terminals.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(dirname "$0")/base-test.sh"

# A second `eval "$(starship init bash)"` after Omarchy's init (a user's own
# ~/.bashrc line from starship's install guide, or re-sourcing ~/.bashrc) should
# neither register starship_precmd twice nor drop the terminal-title entry that
# Arch's /etc/bash.bashrc adds for xterm*/alacritty*/foot*/tmux* terminals.
for cmd in mise starship zoxide; do
  command -v "$cmd" >/dev/null || { skip "needs $cmd on PATH"; exit 0; }
done

tmpdir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmpdir"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$tmpdir/home" "$tmpdir/etc-mise" "$tmpdir/tmp"
: >"$tmpdir/starship.toml"

output=$(env -i PATH="$PATH" TERM=xterm-256color COLUMNS=80 HOME="$tmpdir/home" TMPDIR="$tmpdir/tmp" \
  XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$tmpdir/home/.config" XDG_DATA_HOME="$tmpdir/home/.local/share" \
  XDG_STATE_HOME="$tmpdir/home/.local/state" XDG_CACHE_HOME="$tmpdir/home/.cache" \
  MISE_SYSTEM_CONFIG_DIR="$tmpdir/etc-mise" STARSHIP_CONFIG="$tmpdir/starship.toml" \
  OMARCHY_PATH="$ROOT" bash --norc --noprofile -i 2>/dev/null <<'EOF_SESSION'
PROMPT_COMMAND+=('printf "<title>"')
source "$OMARCHY_PATH/default/bash/init"
eval "$(starship init bash)"
echo "starship_precmd entries: $(printf '%s\n' "${PROMPT_COMMAND[@]}" | grep -c '^starship_precmd$')"
echo "marker"
exit
EOF_SESSION
)

[[ $output == *"starship_precmd entries: 1"* ]] || fail "a second starship init keeps one starship_precmd entry" "output: $output"
pass "a second starship init keeps one starship_precmd entry"
[[ ${output#*marker} == *"<title>"* ]] || fail "a second starship init keeps the terminal-title entry" "output: $output"
pass "a second starship init keeps the terminal-title entry"
```

## Actual output

Merge-base c5b4db77:

```
ok - a second starship init keeps one starship_precmd entry
ok - a second starship init keeps the terminal-title entry
```

PR head a806bfee (the output also shows no `<title>` after `marker`):

```
marker
not ok - a second starship init keeps one starship_precmd entry
```

quattro tip b421b1b4 (mise still first):

```

ok - a second starship init keeps the terminal-title entry
```

Re-sourcing the whole rc twice (separate run with the review fixture, TERM=xterm-256color, a copy of Arch's `/etc/bash.bashrc` plus `default/bash/shell`, `aliases`, `functions` and `init` sourced twice). At the merge-base the title entry survives but `starship_precmd` is already registered twice. At the head it is registered twice and the title entry is gone. Actual output, title escape sequences removed:

```
merge-base c5b4db77:
@@ AFTER_RESOURCE PC_DECL=declare -a PROMPT_COMMAND=([0]="starship_precmd" [1]="starship_precmd" [2]="printf \"\\033]0;%s@%s:%s\\007\" \"\${USER}\" \"\${HOSTNAME%%.*}\" \"\${PWD/#\$HOME/\\~}\"" [3]="__zoxide_hook" [4]="__zoxide_hook")
@@ AFTER_RESOURCE SPC_DECL=declare -- STARSHIP_PROMPT_COMMAND="_mise_hook_prompt_command"
@@ ONE_PROMPT mise_hook_calls=2 starship_precmd_calls=2
PR head a806bfee:
@@ AFTER_RESOURCE PC_DECL=declare -a PROMPT_COMMAND=([0]="_mise_hook_prompt_command" [1]="starship_precmd" [2]="starship_precmd" [3]="__zoxide_hook" [4]="__zoxide_hook")
@@ AFTER_RESOURCE SPC_DECL=declare -- STARSHIP_PROMPT_COMMAND="_mise_hook_prompt_command"
@@ ONE_PROMPT mise_hook_calls=3 starship_precmd_calls=2
```

</details>

<details><summary>Optional notes</summary>

- **Pipeline status:** with a string PROMPT_COMMAND (for example TERM=linux), mise's hook runs before `starship_precmd` at the head and resets PIPESTATUS, so starship gets `--pipestatus=0` instead of `1 0` after `false | true`. Only visible with `[status] pipestatus = true`, which Omarchy's `starship.toml` does not enable; array PROMPT_COMMAND is unaffected.
- **mise-managed starship:** starship embeds the path of the `starship` found at init time. With a starship installed through mise and shims last on PATH (or in a mise `_.path` dir), the head's prompt runs `/usr/bin/starship` while `type -P starship` returns mise's copy; the merge-base runs mise's copy. Tested with synthetic wrappers only.
- **Comment wording:** current mise registers `_mise_hook_prompt_command`, not `_mise_hook`.

**Reproducer: pipeline status**

Tools: bash 5.3.15, mise 2026.9.14, starship 1.26.0, zoxide 0.10.0, run in an isolated sandbox with a private HOME.

With TERM=linux (the virtual console, or any TERM that Arch's `/etc/bash.bashrc` does not list), PROMPT_COMMAND stays a string. At the head it becomes `_mise_hook_prompt_command;starship_precmd;__zoxide_hook`, so mise's function call resets `PIPESTATUS` before `starship_precmd` saves it. `$?` is kept, because mise's hook returns the previous status. Only a starship config with `[status] pipestatus = true` shows the difference; Omarchy's shipped `starship.toml` does not enable the status module. With an array PROMPT_COMMAND (xterm*, alacritty*, foot*, tmux*), bash 5.3 kept `PIPESTATUS` intact across entries in this run, so those terminals are not affected.

Save as `test/shell.d/bash-init-pipestatus-test.sh` and run `bash test/shell.d/bash-init-pipestatus-test.sh` in a checkout. It needs real `mise`, `starship` and `zoxide` on PATH and skips otherwise.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(dirname "$0")/base-test.sh"

# With TERM=linux, Arch's /etc/bash.bashrc adds no title entry, so PROMPT_COMMAND
# stays a plain string. Checks that starship_precmd still records the whole
# pipeline status of the previous command (what starship's status module gets
# as --pipestatus) after default/bash/init has run.
for cmd in mise starship zoxide; do
  command -v "$cmd" >/dev/null || { skip "needs $cmd on PATH"; exit 0; }
done

tmpdir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmpdir"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$tmpdir/home" "$tmpdir/etc-mise" "$tmpdir/tmp"
: >"$tmpdir/starship.toml"

output=$(env -i PATH="$PATH" TERM=linux COLUMNS=80 HOME="$tmpdir/home" TMPDIR="$tmpdir/tmp" \
  XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$tmpdir/home/.config" XDG_DATA_HOME="$tmpdir/home/.local/share" \
  XDG_STATE_HOME="$tmpdir/home/.local/state" XDG_CACHE_HOME="$tmpdir/home/.cache" \
  MISE_SYSTEM_CONFIG_DIR="$tmpdir/etc-mise" STARSHIP_CONFIG="$tmpdir/starship.toml" \
  OMARCHY_PATH="$ROOT" bash --norc --noprofile -i 2>/dev/null <<'EOF'
source "$OMARCHY_PATH/default/bash/init"
(exit 3) | true
echo "pipestatus=${STARSHIP_PIPE_STATUS[*]-unset}"
exit
EOF
)

[[ $output == *"pipestatus=3 0"* ]] || fail "starship sees the previous pipeline's statuses with a string PROMPT_COMMAND" "output: $output"
pass "starship sees the previous pipeline's statuses with a string PROMPT_COMMAND"
```
